question.text: A bullet is shot vertically downwards with an initial velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> from a certain height. Within <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>, the bullet reaches the ground and instantaneously comes to rest due to the perfectly inelastic collision. The velocity-time curve for total time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> will be : (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
As the upward direction is taken as positive, the velocity at t=0 is u=-100 m s-1.

As it is falling under gravity, its acceleration is constant and a=-10 m s-2.

Applying equation of motion for constant acceleration during the time of fall i.e., for 0 to 10 s,

v=u+at⇒v=-100-10×10⇒v=-200 m s-1

After 10 s it hits the ground and remains at rest.

Therefore, option A is the correct representation.
